summary: Steel tower on Jasper Peak near Soudan, Minnesota, built in 1934 on the site of a 1919 wooden lookout; state fire watch into the 1990s.

events.note: First, wooden lookout on the summit, about 10 feet tall, built at the request of forest ranger Fred P. Murphy (local history site; not confirmed by the Register).
Current steel tower. Register and central lookouts say 60 feet; a 1936 survey note says 100 feet.
Land on which the peak stands was bought by the Bois Forte Band from the state; the band later traded it back.

notes_for_editor: Height conflict: Register (60 ft, 18.3 m, used in facts) and Central Lookouts 1934 entry say 60 ft; a 1936 US Forest Service survey note on the Central page says 100-foot steel tower. Not resolved. The Register text misnames the tower once as 'Jacob Peak Fire Tower'; the Register title and the record say Jasper, so treat that as a typo. The 1919 wooden tower and 1996 land sale come only from Lake Vermilion Net, a local history site; not checked against a second source. No dated source after the 1990s states current public access, climbing rules or condition; access and visit facts are left out. Staffing: 'still used into the 1990s' only, so no staffing fact. The Register page credits a photo by Jacob Hufnagle; no new licensed photos found. The NGS-style 1936 note is quoted from the Central Lookouts page.
